newsitem.title: USA: CIGNA Q4 property combined ratio improves.
newsitem.headline: CIGNA Q4 property combined ratio improves.

text.p: CIGNA Corp said the fourth quarter combined ratio for its ongoing property and casualty business improved to 100 percent from 101.5 percent in 1995.
For the year, the combined ratio improved to 101.6 percent from 103.9 percent in 1995, a CIGNA spokesman said.
The combined ratio indicates whether a company is earning a profit on the business it writes. An underwriting profit occurs when the ratio is below 100 percent.
CIGNA said fourth quarter operating income at its ongoing property-casualty business rose to $57 million compared with $49 million a year ago.

For the full year 1996, operating income was $211 million, compared with $128 million in 1995. The ongoing operations had after-tax catastrophe losses of $10 million in the fourth quarter of 1996 compared with $8 million in 1995.
For the full year 1996, the ongoing operations had $48 million of after-tax catastrophe losses compared with $37 million in 1995, CIGNA said.
Amounts for 1995 are reported on a pro forma basis as though the domestic property and casualty restructuring, which was effective as of December 31, 1995, was in place at the beginning of 1995.
These pro forma results are not necessarily indicative of the results that would have been reported had the restructuring actually occurred as of January 1, 1995, CIGNA said.
Consolidated property and casualty segment and international amounts for 1995 were not affected by the restructuring.
The international business had fourth quarter operating income of $33 million, down from $44 million in 1995.
The fourth quarter combined ratio for the international business was 93 percent compared with 92 percent for the same period last year.
For the full year 1996, International had operating income of $135 million, compared with $128 million in 1995.
Domestic had operating income of $24 million for the fourth quarter of 1996, compared with $5 million in 1995.
The domestic combined ratio for the fourth quarter of 1996 was 109 percent, compared with 112 percent a year ago.
For the full year 1996, domestic had operating income of $76 million, compared with break-even results in 1995.
The run-off business had an operating loss of $3 million in the fourth quarter of 1996, compared with income of $18 million for the same period in 1995.
Full year 1996 operating income for the run-off business was $2 million, compared with a loss of $26 million in 1995.
